answer.rationale: Promotional pricing is explicitly contraindicated by memory_73, which shows material 30-day retention damage despite acquisition lift—exactly the wrong tool when churn is already doubling. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well in established customers but do nothing to address immediate churn in price-sensitive SMB accounts now comparing to competitor offers. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) doesn't address SMB base under pressure. Simplify onboarding (memory_31, memory_86) improves activation but doesn't directly counter price sensitivity. In-product activation messaging (memory_91) is the highest-confidence play: it improved week-one engagement and activation with a +1% retention lift, and it compounds with onboarding simplification. The logic is that price-sensitive SMBs considering churn may be responding to perceived lack of product value or unclear path to ROI rather than pure price. Activation messaging can re-anchor perception of product value, potentially reducing defection without retention trade-offs. Running this as a standard experiment on at-risk SMB cohorts preserves learning while limiting downside, and leaves room for follow-on tactics if needed.
